findings.statement: CD70 has an ADC suitability of 0.746 (rank 2 of 2017), surface score 1.0 and a protein log2 fold change of 2.421. Tumour cells expressing it in the weakest quarter of donors are 17.7 percent (median donor 41.2 percent). Staining data are not available (staining_data_available false), so vital-organ safety cannot be judged here.

CA9 (known target control) has suitability 0.647 (rank 13 of 2017), surface score 1.0, kidney staining level 0.0 but vital-organ staining level 3.0 in stomach. Tumour cells expressing it in the weakest quarter of donors are 24.3 percent (median donor 53.3 percent), so a sizeable share of donors is poorly covered.

ENPP3 (known target control) scores 0.578 (rank 39 of 2017) with a protein log2 fold change of 1.544. HPA staining is level 3.0 in duodenum and 3.0 in kidney, which argues against it; 21.3 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors.

SCARB1 is the top-ranked gene in the target profile but has ADC suitability 0.558 (rank 51 of 2017). Staining is 3.0 in adrenal gland and 2.0 in kidney, and only 7.1 percent of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors (median donor 12.4 percent). A high rank in the convergence table does not show a conjugate would work.

SLC16A3 has suitability 0.725 (rank 3 of 2017) and the highest coverage, 43.7 percent of tumour cells in the weakest quarter of donors. However it has 12 transmembrane segments with only 66 extracellular residues, and adrenal staining is 3.0 with kidney 2.0, so antibody access and safety are open questions.

CD70 expression is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (log HR per SD -0.383, padj 0.166, n 88) and on sunitinib (-0.262, padj 0.434, n 89). The difference between arms is -0.121 (padj 0.927), so it is not arm-specific and nothing is significant after correction.

CA9 is associated with longer benefit in all three IMmotion150 arms but none is significant: atezolizumab + bevacizumab -0.112 (padj 0.665), sunitinib -0.336 (padj 0.332). The between-arm difference is 0.224 (padj 0.779). It is not a response biomarker on this evidence.

PCK1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab + bevacizumab (log HR per SD 0.22, padj 0.572, n 88) and slightly longer benefit on sunitinib (-0.069, padj 0.889). The arm difference is 0.289 (padj 0.754); no significant treatment association.

PSAT1 is associated with earlier progression on atezolizumab (log HR per SD 0.164, padj 0.829, n 86) and in the 16-patient nivolumab trial (0.754, padj 0.707). The direction is consistent but no association is significant and the nivolumab set is direction only.

For NNMT the tool returned only the 16-patient nivolumab trial (log HR per SD 0.34, padj 0.782, direction earlier progression with higher expression). No IMmotion150 arm result was returned, so there is no usable trial evidence for NNMT.

EPAS1 returned only the nivolumab trial result (log HR per SD -0.236, padj 0.88, n 16, longer benefit with higher expression), which is not significant and too small to interpret. No IMmotion150 arm result was returned.

CA9 is flagged as a PBRM1 subgroup target candidate: mutant minus wild-type is 0.971 in CPTAC RNA (padj 0.014), 0.335 in CPTAC protein (padj 0.067) and 1.148 in TCGA RNA (padj 7.18e-7). The CPTAC protein difference is not significant, and CA9 is lower in ccB than ccA (TCGA RNA -1.551, padj 1.06e-9).

PSAT1 is not a subgroup target candidate, but it is higher in ccB than ccA (TCGA RNA 2.364, padj 9.07e-39; CPTAC protein 0.541, padj 0.0000157) and higher in BAP1 mutants at RNA level (TCGA 1.711, padj 0.0000578) though not at protein level (0.224, padj 0.396). It tracks the aggressive ccB state rather than a clean mutation.

NNMT shows no mutation-subgroup or ccB-ccA difference: it is not a subgroup target candidate for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 (e.g. PBRM1 TCGA RNA 0.347, padj 0.064) and ccB minus ccA in TCGA RNA is -0.044 (padj 0.82). Its tumour increase therefore looks pan-subgroup.

SCARB1 is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate. PBRM1 mutants are higher in RNA (CPTAC 0.614, padj 0.021; TCGA 0.583, padj 2.98e-6) but the protein difference is 0.306 (padj 0.113), and BAP1 mutants are lower in TCGA RNA (-0.907, padj 0.0000663).

CD70 has an immune target score of 3.384 (rank 20 of 19161). Immune cells make 0.654 of its tumour transcripts, with rho 0.278 with CD8 T cells and 0.228 with regulatory T cells. This conflicts with the tumour-cell reading, and log HR on atezolizumab + bevacizumab is -0.383.

NNMT is not an immune gene: immune cells contribute 0.015 of its tumour transcripts and rho with CD8 T cells is -0.127 (immune score rho 0.08). Its tumour increase is therefore not driven by infiltration.

FCER1G is almost entirely immune-derived (immune share 0.999) with rho 0.898 against the immune score and 0.529 with M2 macrophages. Its tumour-up rank in the biomarker list reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell biology.

FCGR3A has immune share 0.999, rho 0.795 with the immune score and 0.457 with CD8 T cells (immune target score 3.499, rank 13). It is a myeloid and NK signal and should be treated as a microenvironment marker.
CA9 single-cell attribution holds: dominant group RCC in both Li 2022 and Zhang 2021, tumour-cell share 0.976 and 0.981, tumour vs tubule log2 fold change 7.739 and 8.522 (paired donors 4).

NNMT is RCC-dominant in both datasets (tumour share 0.97 and 0.948), tumour vs tubule log2 fold change 9.132 versus 5.573, share-profile Spearman 0.786. The cell call is robust though the effect size differs.

CD70 attribution does not replicate: Li 2022 dominant group is T_NK (tumour share 0.345) while Zhang 2021 gives RCC (0.964). Tumour vs tubule log2 fold change is 6.899 and 5.281. The tumour-cell origin is uncertain.

SCARB1 attribution differs between datasets: Myeloid in Li 2022 (tumour share 0.336) versus RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.582), share-profile Spearman 0.5. The top target-profile gene may be partly non-tumour.

PSAT1 attribution differs: T_NK in Li 2022 (tumour share 0.072) versus RCC in Zhang 2021 (0.78), share-profile Spearman 0.071. Both agree it is lower in tumour than tubule (log2 fold change -4.742 and -3.975).
PCK1 is RCC-dominant in both single-cell datasets (tumour share 0.964 and 0.969) with tumour vs tubule log2 fold change -5.787 and -3.044, consistent with loss of a proximal tubule gene.
NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort: log2 fold change 4.776 (padj 3.07e-46, 86 pairs) versus 2.709 in discovery. Direction and significance agree.
PSAT1 protein loss replicates (confirmatory log2 fold change -3.946, padj 9.71e-23, 69 pairs; discovery -1.963). The one shared phosphosite does not replicate (phosphosites_replicating 0).
SCARB1 protein is higher in tumours in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change 2.334, padj 3.28e-10, 33 pairs) versus 1.837 in discovery; it replicates.
SLC16A3 protein replicates (confirmatory log2 fold change 3.551, padj 1.48e-20, 41 pairs; discovery 2.279) and its one shared phosphosite replicates.
PCK1 protein loss replicates (confirmatory log2 fold change -4.819, padj 3.53e-27, 69 pairs; discovery -1.859) and both shared phosphosites replicate (2 of 2).

caveats: IMmotion150 results are single-gene associations from arms of about 90 patients; none differs between arms after correction, so they are leads, not predictions.
CA9 and CD70 were not tested in the confirmatory cohort (too few matched pairs); this is not a failure to replicate. EPAS1, NNMT and PSAT1 had only partial arm results in the treatment tool.
A high ADC score is not evidence a conjugate would work; CD70 has no HPA staining data, and SCARB1, SLC16A3 and ENPP3 show level 2-3 staining in vital organs or kidney.
Immune-derived genes (FCER1G, FCGR3A, partly CD70) can appear tumour-up through infiltration; the single-cell attribution disagrees between datasets for CD70, SCARB1 and PSAT1.
Zhang 2021 has only 4 paired donors; EPAS1 and the ENPP3, SLC16A3 single-cell and subtype layers were not all queried within the call budget.
